gen-gf-cherry-swash-gf-diphylleia: Diphylleia reads like a classic serif, with openings that hold up even when the text shrinks and stems just heavier than the hairlines. Cherry Swash stands above it with bowls as heavy as its stems, so the heading hits hard and the text settles in beneath.
gen-gf-cherry-swash-gf-donegal-one: Donegal One reads refined, its curves leaving daylight and its thins never spindly. Cherry Swash is best at bold, single-width strokes in every glyph, while the classic serif body does its best work shifting gently from heavy stems to lighter curves.
gen-gf-cherry-swash-gf-fjord-one: Refined and editorial, with a gentle weight change where bowls curve. Over a long passage, Fjord One's wide-mouthed round letters and modest thick and thin rhythm keep each word moving, while Cherry Swash's full-width connections stay up in the heading.
gen-gf-cherry-swash-gf-gentium-book-plus: Cherry Swash cuts a constant-width line, like something etched by laser. Gentium Book Plus, a text serif with horizontals a notch lighter than its uprights and wide openings, gives a longer stretch of reading a mild, pen-like variation.
gen-gf-cherry-swash-gf-gfs-didot: Cherry Swash draws round letters with no tilted stress, and it does that best in large, commanding display lines. But GFS Didot is the one for reading, smoothing the pace with a subtle thick and thin cadence and generous gaps in its curves.
gen-gf-cherry-swash-gf-hahmlet: Dignified and editorial, Hahmlet carries a slight pressure shadow like worn charcoal, with a c and s kept widely parted. And Cherry Swash, monoline in its skeleton, makes the strongest single quality here the clear gap between that bold heading and the subdued serif.
gen-gf-cherry-swash-gf-im-fell-english-s: Bent tubing up top, bookish ink below. And the pair's strongest quality is that tension: Cherry Swash flows from one length of tube, while IM Fell English SC tapers mildly where strokes bend and turn, its serif throats staying open.
gen-gf-cherry-swash-gf-inria-serif: Cherry Swash lays down a unit-width stroke throughout and gives its horseshoe c real swagger up top. Inria Serif follows in a classic serif, with approachable contrast.
gen-gf-cherry-swash-gf-joan: Cherry Swash's diagonals match its stems in weight, which gives the heading its stout, commanding look. And Joan's classic serif text can be sized up a touch, since its gentle weight shifts never turn dramatic.
gen-gf-cherry-swash-gf-junge: Junge reads with authority, its curves generous. Over a long passage, strokes that taper only slightly like a candle flame keep the lines dignified, while Cherry Swash's tubelike, constant-weight lines stay with the heading.
